title: State v. Shehzad & Anr.
court: Addl. Sessions Judge-05 (Electricity), East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
result: Both Shehzad and wife Shaziya convicted u/s 135 (as principals, not abetment); posted for sentence
statutes: Third proviso to Section 135(1) Electricity Act 2003

interpretations.interpretation: Piercing the licensee's pole-mounted service cable to draw supply to unmetered premises is a clause (a) tap; Section 138 was reproduced but only s.135(1)(a) applied. 'Dishonestly' takes its s.24 IPC meaning (wrongful gain/wrongful loss).

Reverse-onus clause: proof of an artificial/unauthorised means raises a compulsory presumption of dishonest use (Neeraj Dutt) rebuttable on the prudent-man standard (Hiten P. Dalal); natural rebuttal is paid bills / lawful metered use, the s.106 Evidence Act onus on the consumer (Mukesh Rastogi).

Inspection power with photo-ID safeguards (60); contemporaneous report, seizure/sealing, photo/video documentation (61); prosecution only where dishonest intention evident + 24-hour police complaint + missing-seal caution (62); assessment at twice tariff up to 12 months with credit for paid units (63). Unchallenged compliance confirms regularity; the Rs. 62,109 assessment measures the theft.

citations.case: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Ashwani Kumar
citations.principle: An inspection report prepared by officers in discharge of official duty carries a presumption of regularity; onus on the consumer to rebut by cogent evidence.

citations.case: Sushil Sharma v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Non-examination of an independent/public witness is no infirmity where inspecting officials are trustworthy and bear no enmity to the accused.
'Shall presume' denotes a compulsory legal presumption the court is bound to draw until the fact is disproved.

citations.case: Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee
citations.principle: Rebuttal of a statutory presumption need not be conclusive; evidence must make the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man.

citations.case: Mukesh Rastogi v. North Delhi Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Easiest rebuttal of the theft presumption is production of paid electricity bills; Section 106 Evidence Act places that onus on the consumer.

significance.point: Both occupants can be convicted as principals
significance.explanation: Spouses jointly occupying unmetered premises fed by one illegal tap are each a 'consumer' and each convicted u/s 135 — no need to route the second occupant through abetment (s.150).

significance.point: Puncturing a pole-mounted service cable is a clause (a) tap
significance.explanation: Piercing the licensee's service cable at the pole to bleed supply is itself the actionable connection.

significance.point: Meters for other floors do not help
significance.explanation: Authorised meters for the building's other floors underscored the absence of any meter for the inspected floor.

significance.point: A filed 65B certificate forecloses the videography challenge
significance.explanation: With Ex.PW1/B on record, planting/fabrication suggestions had nothing to bite on.

significance.point: The reverse-onus presumption binds every occupant
significance.explanation: Neither spouse produced paid bills or lawful-source evidence; the compulsory presumption convicted both.

generic_facts.theft_mode: direct theft — two-core black wire tapped by puncturing the licensee's pole-mounted service cable
generic_facts.premises: 2nd floor of a five-floor building (other floors metered)
generic_facts.occupant_at_inspection: accused Shehzad present; wife Shaziya co-accused
generic_facts.ownership_evidence: ownership documents seized; Shaziya answered s.91 notice
generic_facts.defence: bare denial/false implication; no defence evidence; no settlement
